sentences.text:
Shri Ss Bhadoria - Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri Anurag Sharma - Pp for respondent/State.
Heard on I.A.No.22669 of 2025, which is first application under Section 430 of BNSS/389(1) of CrPC for grant of bail and suspension of remaining jail sentence filed on behalf of all the appellant.

Appellant has been convicted under Section 451 and 376(1) of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for two years with fine of Rs.1000/- and RI for 10 years with fine of Rs.3000/- respectively with usual default stipulations.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant is innocent and he has been wrongly convicted by the Trial Court on the basis of improper appreciation of evidence.
There is delay in lodging FIR.
No person from neighbourhood has been examined as a witness by the prosecution.
With the delay of 5-6 days, the statement of prosecutrix under section 161 of Cr.P.C has been recorded.
The prosecutrix is a married and matured lady.
As per the MLC report, she did not sustain any external or internal injury.
DNA match was not got conducted.

The prosecutrix (PW2) and her husband Mohan Singh Jatav (PW2) have themselves deposed that at the time of incident, the prosecutrix was unable to identify the person who committed rape and she disclosed their names at the instance of the persons who were gathered on the spot after the incident and police has also informed names of accused persons.
All these aspects were not considered 2 CRA-1191-2025 at the time of deciding earlier application for suspension of jail sentence.
The appellant has already suffered jail incarceration for more than one year.
There is a strong case in favour of the appellants.
There are material contradictions and omissions in the statements of the witnesses.
Looking to old pendency of the cases for consideration, final conclusion of this appeal would take sufficiently long time.
Hence, the execution of the remaining part of the jail sentence of the appellants be suspended till the final disposal of this appeal.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposes the application for suspension of sentence and prays for its rejection stating that earlier bail application for the appellant was dismissed on merits.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and taking note of the fact that prosecutrix (PW2) has admitted in her cross-examination that at the time of incident, she could not identify the person who committed rape with her, therefore, it cannot be said that the rape was committed by accused person or not and she has disclosed the name of accused as narrated by the the persons gathered on the spot after the incident, Mohan Singh Jatav (PW3) husband of the prosecutrix

has admitted in cross-examination that his wife/prosecutrix informed him that due to dark at the place of incident, she could not see the person who committed incident with her and police have shown both the accused persons to the proecutrix in the police station, no TIP has been conducted by the prosecution agency, in the MLC report, no external or internal injuries were found and therefore, no definite opinion was given about the rape, DNA has not been got conducted in the matter, the appellant has already suffered jail incarceration for 3 CRA-1191-2025 about one year, and final conclusion of the appeal will also take sufficiently long time, I deem it proper to suspend the remaining custodial sentence of the appellant.

Accordingly, I.A. is allowed and it is directed that subject to deposit of fine amount, if not already deposited, and subject to furnishing personal bond by the appellant in the sum of Rs.75,000/-
(Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of concerned Trial Court
, the execution of remaining custodial part of the sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended, till final disposal of this appeal.
The appellant after being enlarged on bail shall mark his presence before the Registry of this Court on 06.04.2026 and on all such other subsequent dates, which are fixed in this behalf.
List for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.
